556:
## In short

**Jagannātha dāsa**, a poet of **Gilābāḍī** (Maldah), wrote the **Bhakta-caritāmṛta** in four volumes, taking the **Bhaktamāla** as his source.

## Sources

The record's text. Two other Jagannātha dāsas once in this record — the padakartā (#2099) and the one of Pāthara Hājaṅga — have their own records.
1964:
## In short

**Pradyumna Miśra**, of the family of **Kīrti Miśra** of **Buruṅgā** in Śrīhaṭṭa (Sylhet), was a cousin of **Lord Caitanya** — some say a nephew. According to Bimanbihari Majumdar he is not the Pradyumna Miśra of Purī.

## Sources

The record's notes and text.
600:
## In short

**Jayagopāla dāsa**, a disciple of **Sundarānanda**, was the father of **Balarāma dāsa** of the famous **Maṅgala Ṭhākura** family of **Kāṇḍaḍā** (Burdwan); he wrote the **Kṛṣṇa-vilāsa** and the **Jñāna-pradīpa**.

## Sources

The record's text. Which Sundarānanda was his guru is not said. Another Jayagopāla dāsa, guru of Ghanaśyāma dāsa and author of the Bhakti-bhāva-pradīpa, has his own record (#2127).
2121:
## In short

**Giridhara dāsa** was one of the two translators into Bengali of the **Manaḥ-śikṣā** of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī — the other was **Yadunandana dāsa** (Pāṭabāḍī manuscript, Anurāgavallī 24 ka, kha).

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Giridhara Dāsa» #331 until 07-11-2026.
1984:
## In short

**Jagadānanda Ṭhākura**, born in the family of **Śrīnivāsa Ācārya**, had six sons: **Yādavendu, Rādhāmohana, Bhuvanamohana, Gauramohana, Śyāmasundara** and **Madanamohana** (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Jagadānanda Ṭhākura» 4).

## Sources

The record's text.
1993:
## In short

**Jāhnavī-devī** was the mother of **Kāśīnātha (Kāśīśvara) Paṇḍita of Cātarā** (#1832). She went to **Lord Caitanya** at Jagannātha Purī and came back with her son (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Jāhnavī Devī»).

## Sources

The record's notes and text. Not Jāhnavā Mātā, Śrī Nityānanda's wife.
867:
## In short

There were **two devotees named Mādhava** in **Vṛndāvana**, both of whom had come from Bengal; nothing more is known of them (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 13.51).

## Sources

The record's text. Five other Mādhavas once in this record (Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi's friend, the one of Nityānanda's branch, Rasikānanda's disciple, the poet and the Oṛiyā disciple of Gadādhara) have their own records.
981:
## In short

**Narahari Viśārada** — also known as **Maheśvara Viśārada** —, a famous scholar of Gauḍa and a contemporary of **Nīlāmbara Cakravartī**, was the father of **Vāsudeva Sārvabhauma** and of **Vidyā-vācaspati** of Vidyānagara (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 6.53; Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 21.6).

## Sources

The record's notes and text (from «Vaiṣṇava Biographies A-Z»).
2018:
## In short

**Gopāla dāsa** wrote in **1590** a book called **Bhakti-ratnākara**, different from the famous Bhakti-ratnākara of Narahari Cakravartī (Ghanaśyāma).

## Sources

The record's text (from «Vaiṣṇava Biographies A-Z»).
1994:
## In short

**Jāhnavā-devī** was the wife of **Puruṣottama dāsa Ṭhākura**, son of Sadāśiva Kavirāja, and the mother of **Kānu Ṭhākura** (Śiśu Kṛṣṇadāsa, #677). She died soon after his birth, and **Nityānanda** took the child to Khaḍadaha (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Jāhnavā Devī» 2).

## Sources

The record's notes and text. Not Jāhnavā Mātā, Śrī Nityānanda's wife.
2106:
## In short

**Rasamaya dāsa** made a lucid Bengali verse translation of the **Gīta-govinda**; nothing else is known of him.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Rasamaya Dāsa» #1299 until 07-11-2026.
2149:
## In short

**Jagannātha Ghoṣa**, a devotee of **Lord Caitanya**, was the third brother of the famous **Vāsudeva Ghoṣa** (#1654) — the others being Govinda and Mādhava; he left no descendants.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī (Varṣāṇā)» #554 until 07-11-2026.
2153:
## In short

**Lalita Sakhī**, a disciple of **Muralīdhara**, who was related to **Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa**, wrote the **Kahānī-rahasī** in Saṁvat 1835 and the **Kuṁvarī-keli** in Saṁvat 1836.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Lalitāsakhī Dāsī» #837 until 07-11-2026.
2120:
## In short

**Giridhara dāsa** was one of the many translators of the **Smaraṇa-maṅgala** (Pāṭabāḍī manuscript, Bengali B 189, copied in 1681).

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Giridhara Dāsa» #331 until 07-11-2026.
1934:
## In short

**Hemalatā-devī** of **Budhurī** was the daughter of **Śyāmadāsa Cakravartī** and the wife of **Baḍu Gaṅgādāsa** (Bhakti-ratnākara 11.389, 11.399).

## Sources

The record's text. Not Hemalatā Ṭhākurāṇī, Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's daughter.
